reasoning_traces.think:
The tennis scoring system forms a nested hierarchy of probabilistic events: points are Bernoulli trials, games are sums of these trials subject to margin constraints, and sets are combinations of games. The core formula assumes independence between points, which may fail during high-intensity rallies or psychological shifts. Each level introduces complexity—deuce requires conditional logic, tiebreakers alter the baseline probability model, and match outcomes depend on cumulative game probabilities. The derivation proceeds recursively from point-level win probability p to game-level, then set-level, and finally match-level. Dualities emerge in how p and q (opponent's win probability) interact across levels. Failure modes include violation of independence, non-stationary performance, and misapplication of static models to dynamic situations.
